sets.name: Badge
sets.description:
Static, non-interactive status or category label. Type maps 1:1 to the semantic colour tokens (neutral, brand, accent, success, warning, error, info) — the property value and the token family are deliberately the same word. 

Subtle style only; all pairings measured 5.92:1 or better. In code this is variant="{type}"; a `strong` boolean is intentionally not implemented. Not for interactive filters or tabs — those need their own component with hover, selected and focus states.

sets.name: Button
sets.description:
Primary action control. One size (48px) — clears the 44px WCAG target minimum. 

Every variant wraps a 'Button Surface' frame inside a transparent root whose 2px padding is the focus-ring offset; keep that structure so State toggles preserve overrides.

Basic buttons are the most in the interface. Only use another style if a button requires more or less visual weight.

Plain buttons, which look similar to links, are used for less important or less commonly used actions.

sets.name: Breadcrumb Item
sets.description:
A single breadcrumb crumb: a label with an optional leading "/" divider. 

The first crumb in a trail uses Divider=Without; every crumb after it uses Divider=With. 

The current page (last crumb, non-clickable) uses State=Active.

sets.name: Text field
sets.description: Input field that users can type into. A fixed top-left label that stays visible once a value is entered.

sets.name: Dropdown Item
sets.description: A single row inside a dropdown menu (e.g. the Conditions simple list or Services mega menu). Properties: Description (Without/With — toggles a secondary line under the title) and State (Default/Hover).

sets.name: Section Header
sets.description: Headline block used to introduce a page section. Properties: Overline (With/Without), Align (Left/Center), Subheader (With/Without — supporting line under the headline in text/secondary, type/body-large, e.g. "Meet The Doctor" pattern on the live site). All 8 combinations are baked out as separate variants (rather than boolean+visibility properties) so every option is visible directly in the file for design-system browsing.

sets.name: Page Header
sets.description: Top-of-page header used to introduce a page. Always includes Logo and H1 Title. Properties: Breadcrumb (With/Without), Description (With/Without). All 4 combinations are baked out as separate variants (rather than boolean+visibility properties) so every option is visible directly in the file for design-system browsing. Include Breadcrumb on pages with 3+ levels of hierarchy; omit on flat top-level pages.

sets.name: Nav Link
sets.description: Top-level header navigation link. Active shows a 2px brand underline — colour is never the sole indicator of the current page (WCAG 1.4.1). Focus uses the same 2px ring at 2px offset as Button. Hover shifts the label to text/brand. Properties: State (Default/Hover/Active/Focus) and Chevron (With/Without). Use Chevron=With for menu items that reveal a dropdown on hover (Conditions, Services); Chevron=Without for links that navigate directly (About, Testimonials, Web Store).

sets.name: Navigation / Desktop
sets.description: Site header. Height is bound to layout/header-height — 80 on Web, 64 on Mobile — so switching the frame's Dimensions mode resizes it correctly. Logo is fixed left and links to home; nav links sit centre; the booking CTA is fixed right and is the only button in the bar. The phone number is deliberately NOT in the header: the brief's primary goal is shifting volume away from phone. Bottom border only, no shadow, until the scrolled state is designed.

sets.name: Navigation / Mobile
sets.description: Mobile navigation, toggled by the top-bar trigger icon. Properties: State (Closed/Open). Closed is the collapsed top bar (Logo + hamburger trigger); Open is the full-height drawer (same top bar with the trigger swapped to a close icon, plus Nav List, spacer, and Drawer Footer with primary CTA and phone fallback). Distinct from the Desktop Navigation component, which is a separate component due to its structurally different (horizontal) anatomy.
